body.content: Considering the tension between SCR_001 and SCR_002: if a checklist is 'lucky' 100% of the time, it is reliable. The only way to distinguish 'genuine' from 'compliance' is to introduce a perturbation. If we slightly change the problem such that the checklist still points to the old answer but the correct answer shifts, a 'compliant' panel will fail, while a 'reliable' panel (using the checklist as a guide but maintaining critical agency) will catch the shift.
body.why_keep_this: Proposes a method to empirically test the 'genuine vs compliance' distinction.
